entries.body: Oh sailing is so much fun! But it is comfortable, considering we are pushing to windward in 10 knots, flat seas. Left Tobago last night, bound for Martinique, but we won't make it in this wind. Been headed all night, who knows where we will end up? Had a blast in Tobago. Such happy, friendly people, genuinely pleased that you are enjoying their country. We spent a week in Charlotteville, a tiny sleepy little town, so dead we felt like going to sleep every time we came ashore. There was literally nothing to do there. It was incredibly lush and tropical, could have been anywhere in the South Pacific. Then we spent a week at the south end of the island, in Store Bay. Thomas & Brian got in some windsurfing and bought some used gear from the shop there. I enjoyed swimming and the white sand beaches. We could easily have stayed longer. Now we have a long windward trip ahead of us, have to keep moving.

Had a pleasant evening at Savan Island, just south of Mustique. I took a swim, there were a few fishermen living on shore, no lights at night! It was a blue windy perfect morning for a sail but now it's a squally afternoon. We sailed through the Grenadines and past St. Vincent, tacking, but now it's gray, drizzly, wind comes and goes. Can hardly St. Lucia to windward. Plan now is to sail directly to St. Martin, but that may be subject to change without notice! Did 8 knots south St. Vincent with the current, cool.

Ups & downs, and it doesn't do much for Thomas's mood. One minute we're screaming along at 7 knots on our ear, the next, bouncing at 4. I prefer the slow part. Last night was very rough, finally calmed down around 11 am after we sailed behind Dominica. The islands are magnificent. At least the wind has turned in a favorable direction and we are reaching.

Last night was spectacular — the sky was a carpet of stars, shining so bright. We ghosted past Guadeloupe, in the lee, with an endless string of lights along the coast. Flat seas, very light winds, it was worth being awake for! The afternoon had been squally, with the wind up and down. After being becalmed early this morning, it picked up to a comfortable 10 knots and veered to the beam. We are passing Montserrat to windward right now; too bad, since the volcanic lava destroyed the town on the other side, we don't see much. The peak of the volcano is covered in cloud. Guadeloupe is behind us, Antigua is to port. Maybe we will have an easy 24 hours for a change! Should be in St. Martin tomorrow morning.

For once we had a steady 24 hours! We have been beam reaching in 10 knots since yesterday morning, speed up & down, but we are almost here! It has been an interesting sail — right now we are surrounded by islands, the volcano of St. Christophe, St Eustatius, St Barts, Saba, & St. Martin ahead. At least now we can say we have seen all the Windward and Leeward Islands! Looking forward to a week of R&R, more boat projects. Hope it is nice there.

What perfect sailing! We left St. Martin at 5 pm last night, 10–15 knots SE, beautiful! Only problem was all the other boats going all around us. This morning we are passing Virgin Gorda, boats everywhere. St. Martin was okay, good place to stock up on booze, clear water, comfortable. Good French wine, cheese, paté, baguettes. Saw Free Radical there, spent some time with Robert & Claudia on Kamiros. Gave them CHAP, Claudia loved it! Got some boat work done. Not much to do on St. Martin, too many American boats. The Dutch side was awful, like a little Ft. Lauderdale.

Sailing continues good — a bit more wind, but we averaged 6 knots yesterday — not bad dead downwind with no mizzen. Guess we finally found the trades. We were rudely awakened last night, several times by the US Coast Guard calling over the VHF, but it wasn't for us. We have passed Puerto Rico now and are north of the Mona Passage. The water is very blue and the swells are good-sized! Weather is definitely cooler here than in St. Martin.. Go Charlotte!

Wind let off last night & more this morning. There is a cold front passing north of us & we are lucky to have any wind. Will reach south of the Silver Banks tonight. We were here 13 years ago, returning with Lightning and baby Brian. Weather still beautiful, the sea a deep cobalt blue, lots of sun, 10 knots or less.

Another perfect night — moon almost full, seas calm, moving at 5½ knots, no ships! Wind is staying out of the SE so we are still dead downwind. Caught a glimpse of a cape of the Dominican Republic just before sunset. Approaching our waypoint off the Caicos Banks at sunset.
Wind is way down today, and we don't seem to be able to make it past Mayaguana. So I guess we will stop and see what happens tomorrow. Last night was pleasant, with a full moon.

Off to a slow and confusing start today, as the wind turned from NE to NW after we cleared the reef entrance at Abraham's Bay. But now we are passing Plana Keys at sunset, 8 knots NE, calm seas. Loved Mayaguana, the water was fantastic — so clear! The bay was loaded with conch and I snorkeled for hours, even found a lobster. Brian & Thomas had some good windsurfing. The Bahamas are still incredible, best water in the world!

Our companion and friend the Southern Cross has finally left us after 3 years in the night sky. We miss it. The wind is frustratingly light and we are sailing only 3–4 knots. So it will take us 2 days to get to Georgetown. We cross our track today, south of Rum Cay.

April Fools Day and we enter Georgetown harbor, 3 years, 3 months to the day since we left! Fine night, we rounded Cape Santa Maria at midnight, and the Southern Cross was still in the sky! Had to slow down as the wind had picked up, ghosted along until sunrise. Entered at the south end and found Tiama with Helmut & Pauline, and Lalaube with Reiner & Renate, in Red Shanks. What an exquisite little pond to anchor in! The colors are beautiful. We are happy to see Helmut & Pauline again. Now the circumnavigation is officially over!

Wonderful 4 days in Georgetown, too short. Loved seeing Helmut & Pauline again, they never change, just Tiama is more ragged. Helmut spends all his time messing around on the computer rather than fixing his boat! Brian & Thomas got in some good windsurfing. Reiner & Renate on Lalaube were there also, the big Joshua so neat. Went up the hill yesterday to visit Tacelopes again — Ralf, Bergit, John & Pascal. We anchored in Red Shanks which was peaceful, away from the crowds. The town was crawling with American boaters, we are not used to seeing so many. It was such a fun time, we would have liked to stay longer. But the wind was east this morning, time to push north again. Had a screaming sail in Exuma Sound, up to Cave Cay cut. Now we are taking it easy, recovering; stayed up until midnight drinking wine on Helmut's boat. Really enjoy those folks. Thomas caught a big dorado just as we left the blue water.

Got going at 8 am, crossed over the shallow banks by Galliot and out onto the Exuma Banks. Great sailing, fast & comfortable with no seas on a reach. Took the 'Decca Channel' across to the Tongue of the Ocean, even better sailing dead downwind. Sorry to leave the Exumas behind. Will sail overnight past New Providence to the Berrys.

Reached the Tongue of the Ocean before sunset, turned NW to sail past New Providence & up to the Berrys. Lots of wind, never dropped below 7 knots, got a bit rolly once we were past New Providence. Dawn found us off the Berrys, made Great Stirrup by 11 am. Had to abort our attempt to enter the anchorage, tide was running out, wind was blowing on the shoals, and the channel was very narrow, with 2 boats already there. So we went across to Goat Cay, a bit lively but lots of swinging room. Too bad we couldn't keep going, but there's a cold front coming and no other good anchorages past here. We did enjoy the past 24 hours sailing!

Three days went by quickly in Great Harbor. We didn't do much — had a day of blustery wind & rain, a day of sun & wind where Brian had a great windsurfing session, a day of waiting for the wind to turn. Left at sunrise this morning with light NE winds and they died completely. Been motoring almost all day — just passing Freeport Grand Bahama, now, just before sunset. Hoping the wind will come up by dark. The water is incredibly clear and blue.

Yeah — we did get wind when the sun went down! It wasn't much but we were able to flop and bang along all night. Now we are in the middle of the Gulf Stream, doing 4–5 knots with about that much wind. It will put us in Cape Canaveral at sunrise. Too bad our last sail has to be such an obnoxious one, tired of flapping sails. Oh well — Had plenty of this around the world!

Sunrise approach to Cape Canaveral. The wind picked up last night and we ended up under bare poles, doing 2.2 knots. Docked at a marina just before the locks and walked to Customs. No problem at all, they didn't care about anything! Got underway and headed up to Titusville. Thomas is relaxed after 2 years of worrying.

Pulled out of St Augustine, under the bridge before 7 am. Arrived Friday before sunset after 2 long hard days motoring up the Intracoastal, bucking wind & current. Big unexpected cold front, and we have been freezing. Had a good visit with Jason & Lynn, got the car going. Now we are heading to Gibson's Dry Dock up the Jacksonville River to store the boat, if we can make it under the 45' bridge and over the 1.2 meter shoal water to the lift.
